podcast.title: Ex-Sisters of Mercy Members
podcast.body: The Mission featured ex-Sisters of Mercy member Wayne Hussey, and they produced "some great records." Their work was also produced by Led Zeppelin's bassist, John Paul Jones. "There was the mission featuring Existers of Mercy, Dude Wayne Hussie, and they went on to make some great records"

xref.title: First Documented Use of "Grunge" in Music Context
xref.body: In 1981, Mark Arm wrote a letter to a local alternative weekly, "Desperate Times," nominating Mr. Epp and the Calculations as one of the worst and most overrated bands in Seattle, describing them with the phrase "For Grunge, pure noise." This is the first known appearance of the word "Grunge" in print to describe a music style from the American Pacific Northwest, although Arm did not invent the word itself. "In 1981, Mark wrote a letter to Desperate Times, a local alternative weekly that was more of a fan-zene than anything else. To stir things up, the zine invited readers to nominate the worst and most overrated bands in Seattle. Mark took up the mission and wrote this. I hate Mr. Ep in the Calculations. For Grunge, pure noise, everyone I know loves them. I don't know why. This is the first known appearance of the word Grunge in print as a description for a certain style of music from the American Pacific Northwest."

xref.title: Opposition to Music Downloading – Leading the Charge Against Napster
xref.body: Lars Ulrich's most significant impact beyond his musical contributions has been his vigorous opposition to music downloading. He was the public face and the driving force behind the mission to shut down the original Napster, arguing that free music downloading directly takes money from the pockets of musicians and the creative community, whose primary income source is record sales. "Lars was the guy who made an emission to shut down the original Napster For better or worse, he was the guy the public face who led the charge against anyone who downloaded music for free."

xref.title: Semi-Solo Post-Riot Grrrl Supergroup
xref.body: Team Dresch was described as a "semi-solo post-Riot Grrrl supergroup" centered around Donna Dresch. The band continued the mission of the Riot Grrrl movement into a second wave of groups, maintaining its political and feminist edge. "Another group around at the same time, Slater Kinney was Team Dresh. This was a semi-soda post-Ryade girl supergroup built around Donna Dresh."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Unauthorized Sampling Controversies
xref.body: The Jams immediately caused problems by using unauthorized samples from artists like The Beatles and Abba, leading to legal issues. They traveled to Sweden to negotiate with Abba, and upon failure, burned the remaining offending records in a field and threw others into the North Sea. They continued to infringe copyrights, including Whitney Houston's material, before The Jams ended. "He immediately started causing problems by using unauthorized samples in their material, including from the Beals and Abba, which created all kinds of legal problems, which led them to travel to Sweden to try to negotiate with Abba. When that didn't work, they burned the remaining offending records in the field and through the rest overboard into the North Sea as they took the ferry home. Unchastened, they continued to infringe copyrights, the mission and possible theme, material from Whitney Houston and others, and after a few more months, the Jams were brought to an end."
